info.name: DealFlow360 — Team_413 API
info.description:
Complete API for DealFlow360, the Odoo Hackathon 2026 sales-operations platform.

## Getting started

1. Start the backend: `npm run dev` (defaults to port 5050).
2. Seed the first admin: `npm run seed:admin -- admin@teamvector.space "Admin" "S3cure!pass"`.
   The API cannot create an admin — signup always produces a `sales_rep` — so the bootstrap account has to be planted from the backend.
3. Set `EXPOSE_DEV_OTP=true` in `.env` so signup returns the code in the response.
4. Run **01 · Auth → Login (admin)**. Every later request picks up the token automatically from the `staffToken` collection variable.

## Conventions

- Success: `{ "success": true, "data": ... }`, with `meta` on paginated lists.
- Failure: `{ "success": false, "error": { "code", "message", "details" } }`.
- Money is in major units with 2 decimals. Percentages are numbers, not fractions.
- Ids are uuids; `reference` (`Q-1042`, `INV-2031`, `DF-CMC827`) is the human-readable form.
- Request bodies are `.strict()`: an unknown key is rejected with 400 `FIELD_NOT_ALLOWED` rather than silently ignored.

## Two identity spaces

Staff and customers are separate populations. A staff token on `/customer/*` and a customer token on any internal router both get 403 `WRONG_KIND`, checked on every request rather than by hiding buttons in a UI.

request.description: Liveness. Returns uptime.
Checks the database and Redis are reachable.

item.name: 01 · Auth
item.description:
One login surface, two identity spaces. `type` selects which table the credentials are checked against; it is not a privilege — the password still gates entry.

Run **Signup (staff)** then **Verify OTP (staff)**: with `EXPOSE_DEV_OTP=true` the code comes back in the signup response and the collection captures both automatically.

request.description: Always creates a `sales_rep`. A `role` in the body is rejected with 400 FIELD_NOT_ALLOWED — that is what keeps `admin` unreachable from outside.
Six digits, ten minutes, five attempts, single use. Returns a session.
Identical error for unknown email and wrong password, so the endpoint is not an account-enumeration oracle.
The first admin is seeded from the backend with `npm run seed:admin` — never through the API.
Creates a portal account at the lowest tier. Tier is never self-selected — it decides pricing.
The signed-in identity, re-read from the database.
Rotates the pair. Replaying a used token revokes every session for that subject — that is the replay detection.
Always 200, whether or not the address exists.
The new password is checked against the old one BEFORE the code is spent, so a reused password does not burn the OTP.
Revokes every other session on success.

item.name: 02 · Directory (users, roles, teams, customers)
item.description: Reads are open to staff. Role changes are admin-only; team assignment is admin or sales_manager. There is no create-user endpoint anywhere — every account self-registers and proves its own email.

request.description: `role` needs admin; `teamId` and `name` accept sales_manager too. Demoting the last active admin is refused with 409 LAST_ADMIN.
Drives the admin's role picker. `admin` is deliberately absent.
Read-only. Seeded by migration — the brief does not list teams as an admin-configurable resource.

query.description: DF-CMC827, name, contact or email — optional

request.description: With no `q` this lists the directory. A `DF-` term is matched exactly and returns at most one row.
admin / sales_manager only. The one mutation allowed on a customer record — it is commercial configuration, not account data. Existing quotations keep their snapshotted tier.

item.name: 03 · Governance config
item.description:
Tier ceilings, category ceilings and the approval chain. Together these decide what the blended risk score flags and who signs it off.

Reads: sales_manager, finance, admin. Writes: sales_manager, admin. A sales_rep can read none of it — knowing the exact trip points makes it trivial to price a quote to sit one basis point under one.

request.description: Tier ceilings, category ceilings and the chain in one round trip, plus any coverage warnings.
All three at once, so a UI cannot leave bronze above gold between two requests.
`maxScore: null` means unbounded. A rule also matches when any single line is more than `singleLineTrip` points over its own ceiling.
Must list every rule.
Refused when it is the last rule — an empty chain would make every quotation unroutable.

item.name: 04 · Catalog & pricing
item.description:
Every response here carries `costPrice`, so the whole module is staff-only. Reads are open to staff; writes are admin.

Tier pricing is **not** a discount — it is the starting price for that customer, and a rep's discount applies on top and is measured against the ceilings.

request.description: Generates the three tier price rows on create (bronze = list, silver -4%, gold -8%, rounded to 50) so the product is immediately quotable.
`sku` cannot be changed once quotations reference it.
There is no DELETE — a product on a historical quotation must keep resolving.
Copies variants and prices under a new SKU. The copy starts archived so it cannot appear in a rep's picker by accident.

item.name: 05 · Warehouses
item.description: Stock and replenishment. `shippingCostWeight` is the split algorithm's cost tie-breaker — a higher weight means the system prefers to ship from elsewhere.

request.description: Partial map — absent products are left alone, not zeroed. Returns `affectedQuotationIds`: the open backorders this change could now fill, which is what raises the consolidation prompt.
Tops up every product at or below the threshold. Makes the backorder-consolidation path reproducible on demand.

item.name: 06 · Subscription plans & upsell
item.description: A `subscription` product CATEGORY does not make a line recurring — an attached plan does. A product can sit in that category and still be sold as a one-off.

request.description: The two rules are per-plan because they are commercial terms: an annual plan can reasonably refuse refunds where a monthly one prorates daily.
Replace `suggestedProductId` with a different product — a rule cannot suggest its own trigger.
Ranked `coPurchaseScore + (promoted ? 25 : 0) + marginPct * 0.3`. A product whose margin at the customer's tier price falls below the rule's `minMarginPct` is DROPPED, not ranked low.

item.name: 07 · Risk scoring
item.description:
The blended discount risk score. Every line is measured against the stricter of its category ceiling and the customer's tier ceiling; overages are weighted by gross line value.

The worked example below is the one from the problem statement and returns `score 0.21`, `worstSingleOverage 8`, `approvers [sales_manager]`.

request.description: `quotationId` may be null for the admin sandbox. `tierCeiling` and `categoryCeilings` are optional overrides honoured only for admin and sales_manager — a rep cannot score against a ceiling they invented.
A list of 15 rows must not cost 15 requests. Config is loaded once for the whole batch.
Ceilings and chain, for the admin sandbox's starting state.

item.name: 08 · Quotations
item.description:
Prices come from the server. `POST /lines` resolves the unit price from the customer's tier price list and the cost, tax and category from the product.

Lines may only be edited while the quotation is `draft` or `under_negotiation` — anything else would let a rep change the terms out from under an approval already given.

query.description: draft | sent | under_negotiation | pending_approval | approved | fulfillment | billed | confirmed | lost

request.description: A sales_rep never sees another rep's drafts.
The customer must already exist. `ownerId` is optional; a rep may only name themselves. Tier and currency are snapshotted from the customer.

body.raw:
{
  "orderDiscountPct": 5,
  "promisedDeliveryDate": "2026-03-28",
  "validUntil": "2026-04-04",
  "internalNotes": "Customer pushed hard on the setup service.",
  "customerTerms": "Prices valid until the date shown. Payment due 15 days from invoice."
}

request.description: No `unitPrice` — the server resolves it. Adding a product already on the quotation with the same plan increments the quantity instead of duplicating the line.

A negotiated `unitPrice` IS accepted here — agreeing a number on a call is a real commercial act. It is bounded and audited; the cost and category stay server-owned so margin and the binding ceiling remain honest.
Clears `awaitingSeller` and emails the customer.
admin / sales_manager only. Notifies and emails the new owner.
Makes it visible in the customer's portal and emails them. There is no share link and no token — access is by authenticated account only.
Rejects anything outside the transition graph with 409 and a message written for a salesperson.
Applies `counterDiscountPct` to every line, then re-scores and returns both — so the rep sees what accepting the counter costs them in approvals.
Returns a hosted Cloudinary URL, or streams the PDF when Cloudinary is not configured. Customer-facing: no costs, no margins, no risk data.

item.name: 09 · Approvals
item.description:
The rep never chooses the route and never gets to skip it. `submit-approval` re-scores from live line data and resolves the chain from stored config.

Steps are strictly ordered — only the first step still `pending` is actionable. A **return** deletes the chain entirely, so a resubmission re-scores from scratch and a worse quote cannot ride a stale approval.

request.description: Empty body. Either auto-approves (every line inside its ceiling) or opens the chain.
The caller's role must match the step. `admin` may unblock any step so a solo deployment is never deadlocked — and that is audited as an override.
Reason required, minimum 10 characters. Stage becomes `lost`; later steps are marked skipped.
Back to draft, chain cleared entirely.
Only quotations whose CURRENT step matches the caller's role — a finance user should not see one still sitting with the manager.

item.name: 10 · Fulfillment
item.description:
Recomputed from live stock on every read, unless a plan has been accepted or overridden — a rep's deliberate decision is never silently discarded by a recompute.

Ordering: whole-line first, then a warehouse already shipping on this order, then cheapest, then most stock. Subscription and service lines are skipped.

request.description: `canConsolidate` is true when an open backorder could now be filled from current stock.
Moves the stage from `approved` to `fulfillment`.
Returns per-cell errors on 422 so the UI can highlight the exact input, plus `costDelta` against the suggestion on success.
Recomputes from current stock and reports shipments and cost saved.

item.name: 11 · Billing & subscriptions
item.description:
One-time lines produce an invoice; recurring lines produce their own schedule. The two never merge — that separation is the point of hybrid billing.

The preview endpoints do not mutate. The figure is shown to the customer before anything is committed.

request.description: One-time rows, recurring rows with 12 forward occurrences each, and the credit-note ledger.
Generates the invoice and the schedules. Idempotent — calling it twice rebuilds schedules and returns the existing invoice.
No mutation. `explanation` is rendered verbatim to the customer, so it is written in plain language.
Regenerates the schedule and, when the proration is negative, issues a credit note automatically.
Flips future `scheduled` occurrences to `cancelled` and creates the refund or credit note the plan's rule calls for.
finance / admin only, like every other money action.

item.name: 12 · Invoices & payments
item.description:
**The most security-sensitive endpoints in the API.**

Issuing an invoice and recording a payment are finance/admin only: the person who sold the deal must not be the one who confirms the money arrived. Overpayment is refused, the actor is the server's own view of who called, and full settlement moves the quotation to `confirmed`.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header on payments so a double-click cannot record twice.

request.description: `amountPaid` and `balanceRemaining` are derived from the payment rows on every read, never stored.
finance / admin only. Draft → sent, and moves the quotation from `fulfillment` to `billed`. Emails the customer.

header.description: Replaying a key returns the original payment instead of writing a second one.

request.description: finance / admin only. Refuses an amount above the outstanding balance with 422 OVERPAYMENT.
Hosted Cloudinary URL, or the PDF streamed back when Cloudinary is not configured.

item.name: 13 · Customer portal
item.description:
**Authorised against the customer session, never a staff one.** A staff token gets 403 here, and a customer token gets 403 on every internal router.

Every query is scoped by the session's own customer id in the query itself, and another customer's record returns **404, not 403** — a 403 confirms the record exists.

The response is an allow-list built from named safe fields. It never carries `costPrice`, a margin, a risk score, a ceiling, internal notes, the owning rep, the approval steps, or the internal role names.

request.description: Shared quotations only — a draft is never visible.
Permitted whenever `canMessage` — which stays true during internal approval, because a customer waiting on a decision must still be able to chase it.
Either field may be omitted, but not both.

**The automatic re-approval branch.** The server re-scores the final agreed terms and, if approvers are required, puts the quotation back into the chain with no rep action. The score itself is never returned — it is internal governance data.
A draft invoice does not exist to a customer — it returns 404.

item.name: 14 · Dashboard, reports, audit, notifications
item.description:
Alerts are computed on read from live data and the configured thresholds — they are not a queue. Only the operator actions taken against one are stored.

The anomaly rule compares each rep against **their own** rolling 90-day average, not a global threshold: a naturally aggressive discounter would otherwise drown out the signal from a conservative one.

request.description: sales_manager / admin. Notifies and emails the owner.
Notifies every sales_manager and raises the alert to high.
KPIs, per-rep and per-TEAM rollups, discount buckets, funnel and the one-time / recurring revenue mix. Reps with no team appear under "Unassigned" so the team rows always reconcile to the header.
**Append-only.** There is no update or delete endpoint, ever.
